To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
physical activity reduces the risk of CVD in persons with diabetes.

physical inactivity and sedentariness are major risk factors and contributors to CVD in people living with diabetes and that lifestyle interventions that include physical activity can improve CVD risk factors and reduce cardiovascular events in people living with type 2 diabetes, but not in people living with other types of diabetes.

physical activity is associated with reduced risk of CVD in persons with diabetes but that the effect of physical activity on CVD risk in persons with diabetes is less than that in the general population, that the effect of lifestyle interventions on CVD risk is small and that the evidence from clinical trials is insufficient to support a recommendation of physical activity for the prevention of CVD in this population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of physical activities in preventing cardiovascular diseases and diabetes mellitus type II.
the relationship between physical activity and CVD in persons with diabetes.
the role of exercise in the treatment and prevention of diabetes-related CVD, and we believe it will provide useful information for health practitioners and researchers in this field.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
physical activity is not associated with a lower incidence of CVD in individuals with diabetes.
physical activity is beneficial for people with diabetes, but that the benefits for cardiovascular outcomes are less clear.
physical activity is likely to be beneficial for people with diabetes in terms of reducing CVD risk.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
there is no evidence to support a role for exercise in CVD prevention, although the possibility of a role for physical activity in preventing diabetes-related CVD cannot be ruled out.
there is a lack of evidence for a beneficial effect of physical activity on CVD prevention in people with diabetes.
physical activity is beneficial in preventing CVD in persons with diabetes.
The main takeaway from our work is that
although physical activity is an effective strategy for preventing type 2 diabetes, the evidence for its role in preventing diabetes-related CVD is less robust.
physical activity has a beneficial effect in reducing the incidence of cardiovascular events and mortality in people with diabetes and cardiovascular comorbidity.
the evidence for a role for exercise and physical activity in the primary and secondary prevention of CVD in persons with diabetes is not strong, and that further research is required.
